title: Sideband edges
summary: A sideband signal spreads to one side of the carrier. The whole width must stay inside the band or segment.

points.label: LSB near a lower edge
points.value: Carrier 3 kHz above the lower band edge

points.label: 3 kHz USB at 14.348 MHz
points.value: Upper 1 kHz is outside the 20-meter band

points.label: LSB phone on 3.601 MHz
points.value: No: sidebands extend past the segment edge

hook: USB spreads up from the carrier, LSB spreads down. Leave the full signal width between the carrier and the edge.

title: Signal width and purity limits
summary: Rules that keep a signal narrow and clean: width limits by mode, where CW sits on 60 m, and how far down spurious must be.

points.label: CW on a 60 meter channel
points.value: At the center frequency of the channel

points.label: Spurious below 30 MHz
points.value: -43 dB mean power vs the fundamental

points.label: Amplifier certification
points.value: Spurious OK at lesser of 1500 W or full output

title: The two lowest bands: 2200 m and 630 m
summary: Tiny power limits measured as EIRP, plus a notice to the UTC before you transmit.

points.label: Before transmitting
points.value: Tell the UTC your call sign and coordinates

points.label: Waiting period
points.value: 30 days, unless within 1 km of PLC systems

hook: The longer band gets less power: 2200 m is 1 W EIRP, 630 m is 5 W EIRP.

title: Neighbors the rules protect
summary: Some places and services get special protection, and PRB-1 protects you from unreasonable local rules.

points.label: National Radio Quiet Zone
points.value: Around the National Radio Astronomy Observatory

points.label: Antenna near an airport
points.value: May notify FAA and register under Part 17

points.label: 70 cm repeater hits radar
points.value: Cease or change the repeater to mitigate

points.label: Interference to broadcast
points.value: Avoid certain hours on those frequencies

title: Operating on ships and abroad
summary: Which license or permit covers you depends on where you are: a US vessel, Europe, the Americas, or a Canadian in the US.

points.label: Physical control, US vessel
points.value: FCC licensee or alien reciprocal operator

points.label: Ship or aircraft station
points.value: Approved by the master or pilot in command

points.label: CEPT
points.value: US and many European countries, both ways

points.label: CEPT paperwork
points.value: Copy of FCC Public Notice DA 16-1048

points.label: IARP
points.value: Permit for certain countries of the Americas

points.label: Canadian licensee in US
points.value: Canadian terms, not over Extra privileges

hook: CEPT for Europe, IARP for the Americas.

title: What messages may carry
summary: Amateur radio is not for pay or business gain. A few narrow cases are allowed.

points.label: Communications for hire
points.value: Prohibited, except as the rules provide

points.label: Message to a business
points.value: OK if no pecuniary interest, you or employer

points.label: To foreign stations
points.value: Incidental to amateur purpose, personal remarks

title: Rules that start above 222 MHz
summary: Two rules only apply up high: spread spectrum is allowed only above 222 MHz, and Line A closes 420 to 430 MHz in the far north.

points.label: Line A
points.value: Roughly parallel to, south of US-Canada border

points.label: North of Line A, no TX
Spread spectrum
points.value: Only on amateur frequencies above 222 MHz

title: Bands for space stations
summary: Space stations get four HF bands, one VHF band and two UHF bands.
hook: Four on HF, one on VHF (2 m), two on UHF (70 cm and 13 cm).

title: Space station roles
summary: Telemetry reports, telecommand controls, Earth stations talk. Telecommand gets special exceptions.

points.label: Telemetry
points.value: One-way measurements sent from a distance

points.label: Space telecommand station
points.value: Initiates, modifies or ends space station jobs

points.label: Who may be telecommand
points.value: Any station the space licensee designates

points.label: Who may be an Earth station
points.value: Any amateur station, within license privileges

points.label: May be encrypted
points.value: Telecommand signals to a space station

points.label: Posted at telecommand site
points.value: License copy, plus licensee and operator labels

hook: Telecommand is the special case: it may be encrypted and it may be one-way.

title: The exam session, start to finish
summary: VECs coordinate, VEs run the session, and the paperwork goes one way on a pass and another on a fail.

points.label: VEC
points.value: Org with FCC agreement to coordinate exams

points.label: VEC duties
points.value: Keeps question pools, confirms VE applicants

points.label: Who a VE may not test
points.value: Relatives of the VE listed in FCC rules

points.label: During the session
points.value: Each VE responsible; end exam if rules ignored

points.label: Examinee passes
points.value: Three VEs certify; application goes to the VEC

points.label: Examinee fails
points.value: Return the application to the examinee

hook: Pass: three VEs sign and the VEC gets it. Fail: the examinee gets it back.

title: Satellite orbits and modes
summary: A short vocabulary for finding a satellite, knowing its bands, and hearing it well.

points.label: Stays in one spot in sky
Store-and-forward
points.value: Holds digital messages for later download

title: Linear transponders
summary: A linear transponder relays a whole slice of band, so it carries many modes and everyone shares its power.

points.label: Inverting transponder
points.value: Mixes with LO, transmits the difference

points.label: Inverting effects
points.value: Band reversed, USB and LSB swap, less Doppler

points.label: Signals it relays
points.value: FM, CW, SSB, SSTV, PSK and packet

points.label: Why limit your ERP
points.value: Avoid cutting downlink power to other users

hook: Everyone shares one downlink power, so keep your uplink modest.

title: Fast-scan and digital TV
summary: Analog fast-scan copies broadcast TV; digital ATV uses QAM, QPSK and error correction.

points.label: Interlaced scanning
points.value: Odd lines one field, even lines the next

points.label: Vestigial sideband
points.value: AM: one full sideband plus part of the other

points.label: Why VSB
points.value: Less bandwidth, better low frequency video

points.label: Regular TVs on 70 cm
points.value: Use channels shared with cable TV

points.label: Coding rate 3/4
points.value: 25% of data is forward error correction

title: Slow-scan TV
summary: SSTV pictures ride on audio tones: tone frequency sets brightness, and special tones mark new lines and the mode.

points.label: VIS code
points.value: Identifies the SSTV mode in use

hook: Tones carry the picture: tone frequency sets brightness and specific tones start each line.

title: DX, contests and logs
summary: How to work DX and contests, and the formats that carry your log afterward.

points.label: ADIF
points.value: File format for exchanging log data

points.label: LoTW confirms
points.value: US special events, US to DX, WAS: all

points.label: DX QSL manager
points.value: Handles confirmations for a DX station

points.label: Calling in a pileup
points.value: Full call sign once or twice

points.label: VHF/UHF contest SSB, CW
points.value: Weak signal segment, near calling frequency

hook: ADIF to swap logs, Cabrillo to submit a contest log.

title: Amateur mesh networks
summary: Mesh networks reuse Wi-Fi style gear, but amateur rules still apply.

points.label: Frequencies
points.value: Shared with unlicensed wireless data services

points.label: Not allowed
points.value: Messages encoded to obscure their meaning

title: Weak-signal modes by job
summary: Each WSJT mode is built for one hard path: meteors, the Moon, or signals buried in noise.

points.label: JT65 strength
points.value: Decodes signals with very low SNR

hook: Pick by path: MSK144 for meteors, Q65 for the Moon.

title: FT8, FT4 and FST4
summary: These modes take turns on a fixed clock, so your computer's time must be right.

points.label: FST4
points.value: Four-tone GFSK, variable periods, seven spacings

title: APRS
summary: APRS sends position packets that hop from digipeater to digipeater.
hook: In WIDE3-1, the 3 is hops requested and the 1 is hops remaining.

title: HF data modes
summary: HF data trades speed for narrowness: each mode is known for one trait.

points.label: Direct vs audio FSK
points.value: Direct FSK modulates the transmitter VFO

points.label: ALE
points.value: Scans a frequency list, wakes on its call sign

hook: Same four choices, opposite ends: FT8 is narrowest, PACTOR IV moves the most data.

title: Electromagnetic wave basics
summary: A radio wave is two fields at right angles, and its polarization can be fixed, rotating or elliptical.

points.label: Direction of travel
points.value: Right angle to the electric and magnetic fields

points.label: The two fields
points.value: At right angles to each other

points.label: Speed in a medium
points.value: Set by the index of refraction

hook: Right angles everywhere: the fields cross each other, and the wave travels at a right angle to both.

title: HF path geometry
summary: How far a signal goes depends on frequency, takeoff angle, darkness and how it hops.

points.label: MUF drops after dark
points.value: Switch to a lower frequency HF band

points.label: Chordal hop
points.value: Ionospheric hops with no ground reflection

title: TEP and sporadic E
summary: Two seasonal and daily patterns: when each mode opens and how far it reaches.
hook: TEP is an afternoon and early evening mode; sporadic E is a daytime mode, busiest near summer.

title: Moon bounce and meteor scatter
summary: Two ways to reach far on VHF: bounce off the Moon or off a meteor's ionized trail.

points.label: Max EME separation
points.value: 12,000 miles, if both see the Moon

title: VHF and UHF beyond the horizon
summary: Past line of sight: a slightly longer radio horizon, ducts over water, and aurora.

title: Space weather signs and scales
summary: Flares hit fast, geomagnetic storms follow. Know the indexes and scales that warn you.

points.label: 304A parameter
points.value: UV at 304 angstroms, tracks solar flux

hook: Top of each scale is worst: Class X flares, G5 storms. A rising A or K index means more disturbance.

title: Using a digital oscilloscope
summary: Sampling rate sets what a digital scope can show; probe setup and triggering make the trace honest.

points.label: Probe compensation
points.value: Square wave, adjust until tops are flat

points.label: Probe ground lead
points.value: Keep it as short as possible

title: Spectrum analyzers and counters
summary: A spectrum analyzer shows signals by frequency; a counter reads one frequency, only as well as its time base.

points.label: SSB IMD test
points.value: Two non-harmonic AF tones, spectrum analyzer

points.label: Prescaler
points.value: Brings frequency into the counter's range

title: Antenna analyzers and VNAs
summary: Analyzers do the math for you: SWR, impedance and more, after a known-load calibration for a VNA.

title: S parameters
summary: The digits in an S parameter name the ports where it is measured.
hook: S11 stays at port 1, so it is a reflection. S21 involves ports 1 and 2, so it is gain.

title: Receiver noise and sensitivity
summary: Every receiver has a noise floor. Wider bandwidth raises it; the weakest usable signal sits on it.

points.label: Noise figure
points.value: dB ratio of receiver noise to theoretical min

points.label: -174 dBm noise floor
points.value: Perfect receiver, 1 Hz bandwidth, room temp

points.label: Attenuating low HF bands
points.value: Atmospheric noise still beats internal noise

hook: Wider bandwidth lets in more noise: 50 Hz to 1,000 Hz adds 13 dB.

title: Link budget in dBm
summary: Work in dBm: start at transmit power, add every gain, subtract every loss.
hook: Received level is power plus gains minus losses. Margin is how far that level sits above the MDS plus the required SNR.

title: Strong nearby signals
summary: A strong signal near your frequency can deafen a receiver. Know the terms and the cures.

points.label: Desensitization
points.value: Lost sensitivity from a strong nearby signal

points.label: Blocking dynamic range
points.value: dB from noise floor to 1 dB compression

points.label: Reduce desensitization
points.value: Attenuation before the first RF stage

title: Intermodulation and unwanted mixing
summary: Signals mix wherever something is nonlinear, creating new signals that were never transmitted.

points.label: Third-order intercept 40 dBm
points.value: Two 40 dBm inputs make IMD equal to each

points.label: Repeater intermod
points.value: Outputs mix in a final amplifier

points.label: AM broadcast spurs on HF
points.value: Corroded metal joints mix and reradiate

points.label: Reciprocal mixing
points.value: LO phase noise mixes with strong neighbors

hook: Two signals plus anything nonlinear make new signals.

title: Receiver noise and interference controls
summary: Each knob fights one kind of trouble, and some have a side effect to watch for.

points.label: Noise blanker side effect
points.value: Strong signals distort, look like spurs

points.label: Auto notch on CW
points.value: May remove the CW signal too

points.label: Digital noise reduction
points.value: White, ignition and power line noise

points.label: Selectable bandwidths
points.value: Match modulation bandwidth for best SNR

title: Noise sources and fixes
summary: Know each noise by its sound or pattern, then apply the matching fix.

points.label: Switch-mode power supply
points.value: Carriers at regular intervals, wide range

points.label: Car charging system
points.value: Ferrite chokes on the charging leads

title: Phase in inductors and capacitors
summary: Inductors make voltage lead, capacitors make current lead. In a series RLC circuit, whichever reactance is bigger wins.
hook: ELI the ICE man: E before I in an inductor (L), I before E in a capacitor (C). More XL than XC: voltage leads. More XC: voltage lags.

title: Real power vs reactive power
summary: Only resistance turns power into heat. Reactance just stores energy and hands it back.

points.label: Ideal L and C
points.value: Energy stored in fields, power not dissipated

hook: Count only the resistor: 1 A through 100 ohms is 100 watts. The 100 ohms of reactance adds nothing to the real power.

title: Plotting impedance
summary: Rectangular form splits impedance into resistance and reactance. Polar form gives magnitude and angle.
hook: Resistance runs along the horizontal axis, reactance up and down. Capacitive reactance gets minus j; pure inductive sits at plus 90 degrees.

title: Admittance: impedance flipped
summary: Admittance and susceptance are reciprocals of impedance and reactance. Flip the magnitude, flip the sign of the angle.

points.label: Impedance to admittance
points.value: Reciprocal of magnitude, change angle's sign

hook: Impedance pairs with admittance, reactance pairs with susceptance (B). Going across is always one over.

title: Series vs parallel resonance
summary: At resonance the reactances cancel and the impedance is about equal to the circuit resistance. Then series and parallel differ.

points.label: Series reactance voltages
points.value: Can be higher than the applied voltage

points.label: Parallel Q
points.value: Resistance divided by reactance of L or C

points.label: Raising Q
points.value: Internal voltages up, matching bandwidth down

hook: Series resonance builds big voltages inside; parallel resonance keeps a big current circulating while little flows in. Raising Q narrows matching bandwidth.

title: Resonant frequency and bandwidth
summary: Resonant frequency comes from L and C only. Half-power bandwidth is the resonant frequency divided by Q.
hook: Ignore R. Cut C to a quarter (40 to 10 pF) and frequency doubles (3.56 to 7.12 MHz). Bandwidth: 7.1 MHz divided by 150 is 47.3 kHz.

title: Hidden reactance at RF
summary: At RF every part and wire has parasitic reactance. Short leads and the right parts keep it in check.

points.label: Skin effect
points.value: RF near surface, resistance rises with frequency

points.label: Electrolytic capacitor
points.value: Inductance makes it unsuitable at RF

points.label: Short leads, microwave
points.value: Reduce phase shift along the connection

hook: Each part hides its opposite: capacitors carry inductance, inductors carry capacitance. Nominal plus parasitic reactance makes the part self-resonate.

title: N-type, P-type and the junction
summary: Impurities give a semiconductor extra electrons or extra holes. The PN junction between them is what a diode controls.

points.label: Reverse bias
points.value: Holes, electrons pulled apart; depletion widens

hook: N for negative: electrons. Acceptor impurities add holes. Reverse bias widens the depletion region, so no current flows.

title: Semiconductors for high frequency
summary: Two gallium compounds lead for UHF, microwave and MMIC work.

points.label: Why GaAs at UHF and up

hook: Think Ga for gigahertz: gallium arsenide for microwaves, gallium nitride for the very highest MMIC frequencies.

title: Bipolar vs field-effect transistors
summary: Bipolar transistors are run by base current and base voltage. FETs are run by the gate, which has high input impedance.

points.label: BJT beta
points.value: Change in collector current vs base current

points.label: Depletion-mode FET
points.value: Current flows with no gate voltage applied

points.label: Zeners on a MOSFET gate
points.value: Protect the gate from static damage

hook: Bipolar: think currents (beta) and 0.6 to 0.7 V at the base. FET: think gate, with high input impedance and a gate static can damage.

title: The diode family
summary: Each special diode is built for one job. Match the name to its trait.

points.label: Zener
points.value: Constant voltage drop as current varies

points.label: Schottky, strengths
points.value: Lower forward drop; VHF/UHF mixer or detector

hook: Zener holds voltage, varactor varies capacitance, Schottky drops less, PIN switches RF, point-contact detects RF.

title: Logic gates and truth tables
summary: Positive logic makes high a 1. Each gate is then just a rule for when its output is 1 or 0, listed in a truth table.

points.label: Positive logic
points.value: High voltage is 1, low voltage is 0

points.label: Truth table
points.value: Lists inputs and the matching outputs

points.label: NAND
points.value: Output 0 only if all inputs are 1

points.label: Two-input XNOR
points.value: Output 0 if one and only one input is 1

hook: The N means NOT: NAND is AND flipped (0 only when all inputs are 1), and XNOR is XOR flipped (0 when exactly one input is 1).

title: Logic thresholds and output states
summary: Digital parts decide by comparing to a threshold and drive defined output states. Each row keeps that decision clean.

points.label: Comparator hysteresis
points.value: Stops input noise causing unstable output

points.label: CMOS noise immunity
points.value: Switching threshold about half the supply

points.label: BiCMOS
points.value: CMOS input impedance, bipolar output impedance

points.label: Pull-up or pull-down
points.value: Sets a voltage when a pin is open circuit

hook: Threshold in the middle means noise must swing far to flip a bit. A pin that floats needs a pull-up or pull-down to stay defined.

title: Inductor core materials
summary: The core's permeability sets inductance. Material and shape decide stability, losses and how far the field strays.

points.label: Ferrite vs powdered iron
points.value: Ferrite needs fewer turns for same inductance

points.label: Thin layers
points.value: Reduce power loss from eddy currents

points.label: Toroid vs solenoid
points.value: Toroid confines most of the field in the core

hook: Ferrite is strong (fewer turns), powdered iron is steady (temperature stable), brass works backward (less inductance).

title: Piezoelectricity both ways
summary: Piezoelectric materials turn stress into voltage and voltage into motion. That is what makes a quartz crystal resonate.

points.label: Quartz crystal equivalent
points.value: Series RLC in parallel with a shunt C

hook: Squeeze it, get volts. Give it volts, it moves.

title: Through-hole vs surface mount
summary: Long leads add parasitics. That keeps DIP parts off UHF and makes surface mount the RF choice.

points.label: DIP layout
points.value: Two rows of pins on opposite sides

points.label: Surface mount at RF
points.value: Smaller, shorter traces, less parasitic L and C

hook: Shorter is better at RF: DIP leads are too long for UHF, surface mount has the least parasitics.

title: MMIC amplifier basics
summary: An MMIC is a ready-made VHF to microwave gain block with a standard impedance, fed and connected in standard ways.

points.label: Why popular
points.value: Controlled gain, low noise, constant impedance

points.label: DC power
points.value: Resistor and/or RF choke on the output lead

hook: 50 ohms in, 50 ohms out, over microstrip, with DC fed through the output lead.

title: Photovoltaic cells
summary: A photovoltaic cell converts light to electrical energy. Most are silicon and give about half a volt each.

points.label: Photovoltaic effect
points.value: Conversion of light to electrical energy

points.label: Efficiency
points.value: Fraction of light converted to current

hook: Light hits electrons, electrons make current. A silicon cell gives 0.5 V when fully lit.

title: Devices controlled by light
summary: Light can lower a resistance, carry a signal across an isolation gap, or count the turns of a shaft.

points.label: Optoisolator with 120 VAC
points.value: Isolates control circuit from switched circuit

points.label: Optical shaft encoder
points.value: Patterned wheel interrupts a light source

hook: More light, less resistance. In an optoisolator only light crosses the gap, keeping the control side isolated from the 120 VAC side.

title: Multivibrators and counters
summary: Digital timing circuits are named by how many stable states they have, and flip-flops chain into dividers.

points.label: Decade counter
points.value: One output pulse for every 10 input pulses

points.label: Monostable
points.value: Switches to an alternate state for a set time

points.label: Astable
points.value: Keeps alternating, no external clock needed

hook: Each flip-flop halves the rate, so 4 in a row divide by 16. The prefix counts stable states: bistable two, monostable one, astable none.

title: Amplifier classes: linear to switching
summary: Class A sits in the middle of its range; switching classes slam between saturation and cutoff for efficiency.

points.label: Class AB, push-pull
points.value: Each side conducts over 180, under 360 degrees

points.label: Why switching is efficient
points.value: Device at saturation or cutoff most of the time

points.label: Switching amplifier output
points.value: Needs a filter to remove harmonic content

hook: Linear classes keep the device in its middle range; switching classes live at the extremes, which saves power but makes harmonics to filter.

title: Amplifier configurations and bias
summary: Name the shared terminal and you know the circuit. Figure E7-1 is a common emitter stage with two kinds of bias.

points.label: Emitter follower
points.value: Common collector: input and output in phase

hook: A follower follows: its output tracks the input, in phase.

title: LC networks: Pi, Pi-L and T
summary: Where the inductors and capacitors sit decides what passes. Matching networks also cancel reactance.

points.label: Low-pass Pi
points.value: Shunt capacitors at each end, series inductor

points.label: Pi-L network
points.value: A Pi with an added output series inductor

points.label: Impedance matching
points.value: Cancels reactance, sets resistance to target

hook: A series inductor blocks highs, so the Pi is low-pass. Series capacitors block lows, so that T is high-pass.

title: Filter types and where they fit
summary: Each filter family has a signature trait or a typical home in the station.

points.label: Chebyshev
points.value: Ripple in the passband, sharp cutoff

points.label: Elliptical
points.value: Extremely sharp cutoff, notches in stop band

points.label: Crystal lattice
points.value: For low-level signals, made of quartz crystals

points.label: Helical
points.value: Band-pass or notch in VHF and UHF radios

title: Linear vs switching regulators
summary: A linear regulator burns off the excess voltage as heat; a switcher chops it with pulses and filters the result.

points.label: Series regulator heat
points.value: (Input minus output voltage) x output current

points.label: Switchmode regulator
points.value: Varies duty cycle of pulses into a filter

hook: Linear: the voltage you drop times the current you pass is heat. Switching: high frequency lets the magnetics shrink.

title: Linear regulator building blocks
summary: A Zener sets the reference, then a series or shunt element holds the output. Figure E7-2 puts it together.

points.label: Shunt regulator
points.value: Works by loading the unregulated source

points.label: Q1 in E7-2
points.value: Controls current to keep output voltage constant

points.label: C2 in E7-2
points.value: Bypasses rectifier output ripple around D1

title: Making and detecting each mode
summary: Every mode has a circuit that creates it and one that recovers it. Learn them as pairs.

points.label: Make FM
points.value: Reactance modulation of a local oscillator

points.label: Reactance modulator
points.value: Varies a capacitance to make PM or FM

points.label: Make SSB
points.value: Balanced modulator followed by a filter

points.label: Diode envelope detector
points.value: Rectifies and filters the RF signal

title: From baseband to RF
summary: The message starts at baseband, gets shaped for FM, then a mixer moves it in frequency.

points.label: Pre-emphasis
points.value: Boosts higher audio frequencies in FM speech

points.label: Mixer output
points.value: Both inputs plus their sum and difference

hook: Pre-emphasis boosts highs on the way out; de-emphasis undoes it on the way in.

title: Sampling and sample rate
summary: Sample fast enough and filter out what you cannot sample. The sample rate sets how much spectrum an SDR sees.

points.label: Minimum sample rate
points.value: At least twice the highest frequency

points.label: Direct sampling
points.value: RF digitized by an ADC with no mixing

points.label: Decimation
points.value: Removes samples to cut the sample rate

points.label: Anti-alias filter
points.value: Stops highs showing up as lower frequencies

hook: Twice the highest frequency is the floor. Anything above that must be filtered out first, or it folds back as a false lower frequency.

title: ADC and DAC: bits and quality
summary: Bits set how finely a converter measures. Dither and filters clean up the steps it leaves behind.

points.label: Smallest detectable signal
points.value: Reference voltage and sample width in bits

points.label: Dither
points.value: Small noise added to reduce quantization noise

points.label: Flash ADC in an SDR
points.value: Very high speed digitizes high frequencies

hook: Each added bit doubles the levels: 8 bits give 256. Ten bits are needed to split 1 volt into 1 millivolt steps.

title: Time domain and frequency domain
summary: The same signal can be seen as amplitude over time or as a set of frequencies. Fourier tools move between the two.

points.label: Fourier analysis
points.value: Square wave is a sine plus its odd harmonics

title: DSP filters and digital SSB
summary: Digital filters are built from delay taps; the same math also generates and cleans up SSB.

points.label: Taps
points.value: Incremental signal delays for the algorithm

points.label: FIR filters
points.value: Can delay all frequencies by the same amount

hook: More taps, more delays to work with, sharper filter.

title: Op-amp traits
summary: An op-amp is a near ideal amplifier: huge gain, very high input impedance, very low output impedance.

points.label: Gain-bandwidth
points.value: Frequency where open-loop gain equals one

points.label: Input offset voltage
points.value: Differential input that zeroes open-loop output

hook: High in, low out: it barely loads what feeds it and easily drives what follows.

title: Inverting op-amp gain (Figure E7-3)
summary: In Figure E7-3 the gain is RF divided by R1, and the output is inverted.
hook: Divide RF by R1: 470 / 10 = 47. The sign flips, so 0.23 volts in becomes -2.3 volts out.

title: Oscillators and stability
summary: Oscillators differ in how they feed back, and good ones fight drift from heat and vibration.

points.label: Crystal on spec frequency
points.value: Give it the specified parallel capacitance

points.label: Reduce microphonics
points.value: Mechanically isolate it from its enclosure

hook: Colpitts uses Capacitors; Pierce uses a crystal.

title: Frequency synthesizers: PLL and DDS
summary: A PLL locks an oscillator to a reference; a DDS builds the waveform from a table of numbers.

points.label: Phase-locked loop
points.value: Phase detector, low-pass filter, VCO, reference

points.label: Direct digital synthesizer
points.value: Phase accumulator, lookup table, DAC, filter

points.label: DDS lookup table
points.value: Amplitude values of the desired waveform

title: FM modulation index and deviation ratio
summary: Both are deviation divided by audio frequency. Divide and you have the answer.

points.label: PM index vs carrier
points.value: Does not depend on the RF carrier frequency

title: Multiplexing: sharing a channel
summary: Signals can share a transmission by splitting it into frequency bands, time slots, or orthogonal subcarriers.

points.label: Frequency division (FDM)
points.value: Separate bands, each a different data stream

title: Symbols, baud and QAM
summary: A symbol is one change of the waveform. QAM and QPSK states are mapped on a constellation diagram.

points.label: Symbol rate
points.value: Rate the waveform changes to carry information

points.label: Constellation diagram
points.value: Possible phase and amplitude states per symbol

points.label: More data, same bandwidth
points.value: Use a more efficient digital code

title: Digital signal bandwidths
summary: Three widths to know, from narrow CW and FT8 up to fast FM data.
hook: Slow CW (52 Hz) and FT8 (50 Hz) are nearly the same width; fast FM data is hundreds of times wider.

title: Keeping signals clean and narrow
summary: Sharp edges and overdriven audio both spread a signal. Soften the edges and keep audio levels down.

points.label: CW bandwidth depends on
points.value: Keying speed and rise and fall time

points.label: PSK phase change timing
points.value: At the zero crossing, to minimize bandwidth

hook: Abrupt changes splatter. Smooth the keying, change phase at zero, and keep the audio down.

title: Digital codes and error control
summary: Codes define the bits per character; parity and ARQ catch and fix errors.

points.label: Gray code
points.value: Only one bit changes between values

points.label: Parity bits
points.value: Some types of errors can be detected

points.label: ARQ
points.value: Requests a retransmission when errors are found

hook: Parity only detects errors; ARQ fixes them by asking again.

title: Spread spectrum techniques
summary: Spread spectrum spreads a signal by an algorithm; the receiver suppresses anything not using it.

points.label: Direct sequence
points.value: High-speed bit stream shifts the carrier phase

points.label: Interference resistance
points.value: Signals not using the algorithm are suppressed

title: Antenna gain and ERP
summary: Start from transmitter power, subtract every loss, add antenna gain, and convert the net dB to watts.

points.label: Isotropic radiator
points.value: Lossless, equal in all directions, the reference

points.label: Gain antenna vs isotropic
points.value: Total radiated power is the same

hook: Net dB is gain minus losses: 150 W at +2.8 dB is about 286 W. Gain only redirects power, it never adds to the total.

title: How ground shapes an antenna
summary: The ground under an antenna changes its losses, its impedance and the angle its signal leaves at.

points.label: Horizontal above a slope
points.value: Takeoff angle lower in downhill direction

hook: Radials fight lossy soil and seawater boosts low angles. Raising a horizontal antenna, or a downhill slope, lowers its takeoff angle.

title: Short antennas and loading
summary: A shortened antenna is resonated with a coil. Efficiency and bandwidth both depend on how it is done.

points.label: Best coil location
points.value: Near the center of the vertical radiator

hook: Efficiency is radiation resistance over total resistance, so keep coil losses low. Loading and high Q both narrow SWR bandwidth.

title: Reading radiation pattern plots
summary: Read each plot by comparing the main lobe with the back, the sides, or the half-power points.

points.label: Far field
points.value: Pattern shape no longer varies with distance

title: Antenna modeling
summary: Modeling software chops wires into segments; too few segments give wrong answers.

points.label: Principle
points.value: Wire as segments, each with uniform current

points.label: Under 10 per half wavelength
points.value: Feed point impedance may be incorrect

title: Phased vertical arrays
summary: Two quarter-wave verticals: spacing and feed phase decide where the pattern points.

points.label: 1/2 wave apart, in phase
points.value: Figure-eight broadside to the array axis

hook: In phase fires broadside; 180 degrees out fires along the axis; a quarter wave with 90 degrees makes a one-way cardioid.

title: Dipole family wire antennas
summary: Each of these is a dipole with a twist: folded, end-fed, extended, or fed off center.

points.label: Folded dipole
points.value: Half-wave dipole plus a parallel wire

points.label: G5RV
points.value: Center-fed via open-wire line, balun, coax

points.label: Off-center-fed dipole
points.value: Similar feed impedance on multiple bands

title: Yagi design
summary: One driven element plus parasitic elements tuned long or short to steer the phase.

points.label: Circular polarization
points.value: Two Yagis at right angles, fed 90 degrees apart

title: Antenna matching systems
summary: Each matching system has a signature: where it connects and what reactance it needs or cancels.

points.label: Gamma match
points.value: Shield at center, conductor off to one side

points.label: Beta or hairpin
points.value: Driven element insulated from the boom

points.label: Stub match
points.value: Short line in parallel near the feed point

points.label: Wilkinson divider
points.value: Splits power equally into two 50 ohm loads

title: Velocity factor and line types
summary: Waves travel slower in a line than in a vacuum, so lines are electrically longer than they look.

points.label: Velocity factor
points.value: Wave speed in line / speed of light

points.label: Coax electrically longer
points.value: Waves move more slowly than in air

title: Shorted and open line sections
summary: A line section's length and end condition decide what the generator sees.
hook: A quarter wave flips the end: short looks high, open looks low. A half wave shows the short as it is.

title: The Smith chart
summary: A map of impedance: resistance circles, reactance arcs, and scales in wavelengths for working along a line.

points.label: Common uses
points.value: Impedance, SWR, and matching stub placement

hook: Arcs are reactance and end on the outer reactance axis; the one straight line is the resistance axis.

title: Low-band receiving and terminated wires
summary: On the low bands noise is high, so receiving antennas chase directivity. A terminating resistor makes a wire one-way.

points.label: 160 and 80 meter receiving
points.value: Directivity matters much more than losses

points.label: RDF
points.value: Peak gain vs average over the hemisphere

points.label: Beverage termination
points.value: Absorbs signals from the reverse direction

points.label: Right termination value
points.value: Minimum SWR variation over the range

points.label: Longer unterminated wire
points.value: More lobes, major lobes nearer the wire axis

title: Direction-finding loops
summary: A small loop has two nulls. DF work adds tricks to get a single null and deeper nulls.

points.label: Sense antenna
points.value: Gives a null in only one direction

points.label: More loop output voltage
points.value: More turns and/or more enclosed area

title: RF exposure rules
summary: Exposure is judged against MPE limits, strictest from 30 to 300 MHz. Know who must act and what is exempt.

points.label: Multiple transmitters
points.value: Each at 5 percent or more of its MPE limit

points.label: SAR
points.value: Rate RF energy is absorbed by the body

points.label: Station on 80 meters
points.value: An evaluation must always be performed

title: Tower climbing safety
summary: Tower work: a ground rod for lightning, then stay tied off at all times, lanyards on the legs, the shock-absorbing one up high.

points.label: 100% tie-off
points.value: At least one lanyard attached at all times
